_comment: Every noise the game can make, by id — nothing outside this file names an audio path. A level or pack may name its own manifest, which is laid over this one, so retuning a single sound is a file this size rather than a copy of all of them, and an entry of null silences that one. A def is one of three things. A synthesized shape: wave (oscillator type), sweep ([[hz, seconds], ...] for one note bending through those pitches), notes ([hz, ...] for separate notes `step` seconds apart), gain (peak volume), attack (seconds to reach it, 0 starts there), decay (seconds to fade back to silence), noise (an extra burst of static over the top). A recorded one-shot: src naming a .wav or .mp3, resolved against this manifest, with gain scaling it. Or a track: src plus loop true, which is what a level's "music" id picks. `shake` is how long the phone buzzes with it, since every sound in the game is a response to something the player just did.
